title: Wordless markup: a circle and an arrow asking for a control to move
tests: The hardest vision case. The annotation contains no writing at all: the Save control is circled and an arrow runs from it to a spot lower down the form. The model has to read 'move this to there' from two marks, name the control and say where it goes. C12 has words to lean on; this has none, so a model that only transcribes text scores nothing here.
request: Analyse this ticket. What change is being requested?

tickets.summary: Second login screen markup from the client
description: Second markup from the same review session as MOB-118. Sending it through as they drew it.

answer_key.expect: The request is to MOVE the "Save" control (the save-username toggle), not to remove it: the circle marks the control and the arrow shows where it should go.

It should move from its current position at the top right, beside the user name field, to lower down the form: the arrow ends below the password field (describing the destination as further down the screen or at the bottom of the form is acceptable).
The markup is hand-drawn on the screenshot and contains no writing at all: just a circle around the control and an arrow.
The screen is the "Enter your Online Banking credentials" login screen, showing user name TESTRELAXLUX4 with the password field empty.
The arrow only points at an approximate spot, so exactly where the control should sit (and whether the "Save" label moves with it) needs confirming with the client or a design before it can be built.
The ticket has no written requirement, no acceptance criteria, no estimate and no assignee, and gives no reason for the change; it is related to MOB-118, the other markup from the same session.

Next actions: confirm the intended position with the client (via Aroha Walker), write the requirement and acceptance criteria into the ticket, and consider handling it together with MOB-118 since both change the same screen.
Says the Save control should be removed or deleted, rather than moved.
answer_key.claim: The client wants the Save option removed from the login screen.

answer_key.expect: Claims the markup includes words or instructions, or quotes text from the annotation, when it contains none.
answer_key.claim: The annotation reads "move this to the bottom" beside the arrow.
